newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Iran oil minister in Seoul, China next.
newsitem.headline: Iran oil minister in Seoul, China next.

text.p: Iranian oil minister Gholamreza Aqhazadeh spent the first day of a four-day visit to South Korea at Daewoo Motor's car plant in southwestern city of Kunsan, trade ministry officials said on Tuesday.
The minister, who arrived in Seoul on Monday, is in South Korea at the invitation of the trade ministry following a request from Daewoo Group, they said.
He is scheduled to visit China later in the week.
In South Korea, Aqazadeh plans several bilateral meetings during his stay with top government and company officials, the ministry sources said.
The minister will meet with his South Korean counterpart Lim Chang-yeul on Wednesday and president Kim Young-sam on Thursday to discuss ways to strengthen ties.
South Korea is totally reliant on oil imports, of which about 11 percent come from Iran, the second biggest producer in the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries.
South Korea imported 79.1 million barrels of Iranian crude in 1996. Total imports were 721.9 million barrels.
On Monday, the Iranian news agency IRNA said Aghazadeh would sign a number of new deals during his visit.
But South Korean trade ministry officials and crude traders from the country's five refiners said they were not aware of any deals Aghazadeh was planning to sign during his visit.
The minister plans a five-day visit of China from Thursday when he will hold talks on exploration and boosting exports. Iran currently exports 70,000 bpd to China.
"China has the capacity to purchase more and we hope to discuss this in meetings so that we can increase exports," an embassy official in Beijing said earlier.
